message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"96dc64ee482f413c5449de7631be7d0eb6c53021a4a1b69dbd8d075d4285d263","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ca-class-c:lineage:74","source_registry_sha256":"bc7054e4d59fbb00e9f8cd8f658a743fe5db5406dc1e5275d4d2375fe6e19182","units":[{"unit_id":"sec02-u01","module_id":"sec02-m01","objective_ids":["sec02-u01"],"title":{"text":"Permit first, then the proofs","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"An application missing one proof stalls the whole permit, so knowing all four saves a return trip.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05"]},{"text":"Without any license, the permit is the gate to the drive test.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Rosa has never held a license and her passport shows her maiden name, while her application uses her married name.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F04"]},"reasoning":{"text":"She needs a permit before any drive test, and a name mismatch calls for a legal full name document on top of identity, residency and social security proofs.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05"]},"result":{"text":"Rosa brings identity proof, two residency proofs, her social security number and a legal name document, then applies for the permit.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking one proof of where you live is enough.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03"]},"correction":{"text":"The application needs two proofs that you live in California, though exceptions may apply.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-R02"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Who, where twice, which name, which number.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"An applicant's identity document shows a different name from the application. Which extra document fixes that?","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-R02"]},"answer":{"text":"A legal full name document proving the current name.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04"]},"rationale":{"text":"When the names differ, the legal full name document bridges the gap; identity, residency and social security proofs are still needed too.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-R02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Starting from no license","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"No license yet means a permit first.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05"]},{"text":"The application carries several proofs.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson starts at the very beginning of the path to a California license. If you do not have a license from California or another state, you must hold an instruction permit before you may take the behind-the-wheel drive test. Getting that permit begins with an application, and the application has to carry proofs. We will look at proof of identity, the proofs that you live in California, the legal name document for mismatched names, and the social security number. We will also see where REAL ID rules are posted and who handles voter registration, so you know where each question belongs.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Identity and residency","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Proof of identity shows who you are.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},{"text":"Two proofs show you live in California.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every permit or license application must include proof of identity, a document showing who you are. Alongside it, you must show two proofs that you live in California, although exceptions may apply. Notice the number: residency takes two proofs, not one. Identity answers the question of who you are, and residency answers the question of where you live. They are separate jobs, so one document does not cover both. When you gather your paperwork, make sure you have your identity proof and both residency proofs ready, and check whether any exception applies to your situation before you go.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Names and numbers","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Mismatched name: add a legal name document.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-R02"]},{"text":"A social security number is required.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Two more proofs round out the application. First, when the name on your identity document differs from the name on your application, you must add a legal full name document proving your current name. That document is the bridge between the two names. Second, a social security number is required as well, with exceptions possible. Put together, the four proofs do four jobs: identity says who you are, the two residency proofs say you live in California, the name document bridges mismatched names, and the social security number identifies the record. Keep each job separate in your mind.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"A worked example","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Rosa has no license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-R02"]},{"text":"Her passport shows a different name.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a worked example. Rosa has never held a license, and her passport shows her maiden name while her application uses her married name. What does she need? Because she has no license from any state, she needs an instruction permit before any drive test. For the application she brings proof of identity, two proofs that she lives in California, and her social security number. Because the names differ, she also adds a legal full name document proving her current name. With all four proofs in hand, Rosa can move on to the permit steps without being sent home to fetch a missing paper.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"One residency proof?","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: one proof of address is enough.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-R02"]},{"text":"Truth: two residency proofs are required.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap that catches many applicants. People often bring a single document showing where they live and assume that settles residency. The handbook asks for two proofs that you live in California, though exceptions may apply. A second trap is assuming the identity document alone takes care of a name change. It does not. When the name on your identity document differs from your application, you must add a legal full name document. So count your proofs carefully: one for identity, two for residency, a name document if the names differ, and your social security number.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-R02","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"The names do not match.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-R02","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F05"]},{"text":"Which extra document fixes it?","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-R02","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: an applicant's identity document shows a different name from the one on the application. Which extra document fixes that? Settle on your answer. The answer is a legal full name document proving the current name. That document bridges the gap between the two names. It does not replace the other proofs, so the applicant still needs proof of identity, two proofs of California residency, and a social security number. If you named the legal full name document, you have the four-proofs idea. If not, review which proof does which job in this lesson.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-R02","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Proofs and where to ask","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R02","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Four proofs, four jobs.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R02","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},{"text":"REAL ID and voting have their own homes.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R02","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, remember the starting rule: with no license from any state, you need an instruction permit before the behind-the-wheel drive test. The application carries proof of identity, two proofs of California residency, a legal full name document when names differ, and a social security number. Two related questions live elsewhere. Current REAL ID document rules and eligibility are posted on the DMV REAL ID page, and voter registration runs through the California Secretary of State. With your proofs sorted, the next lesson walks through the ordered steps of the Class C permit itself.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R02","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u02","module_id":"sec02-m02","objective_ids":["sec02-u02"],"title":{"text":"Steps permit.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-R03"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the fee and documents count as tests.","fact_ids":["sec02-R03"]},"correction":{"text":"The permit?","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-R03"]},"answer":{"text":"The knowledge test or tests and the vision test.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10"]},"rationale":{"text":"Paperwork comes first, and the permit then needs a pass on the knowledge test or tests and the vision test.","fact_ids":["sec02-R03","sec02-F10"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"The road to a first, tests after.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"In this lesson we walk through the steps to a Class C instruction permit. If you hold no license, the permit comes before any drive test, and the permit itself follows a clear order. You start with an application, then you hand over documents and pay a fee, and then you pass tests. Knowing the order matters because each step depends on the one before it. We will go through each step, separate the paperwork from the tests, and point you to the DMV page that lists the full set of permit steps and requirements in one place.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Application, documents, fee","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Complete the application form.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R03"]},{"text":"Hand over documents.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R03"]},{"text":"Pay a non-refundable fee.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"A Class C permit starts with a completed Driver's License and ID Card Application. That form is step one. Next you hand over your documents and pay an application fee. Note that the fee is non-refundable, so it is not returned if you change your mind or need another try. These first steps are paperwork. They prepare your file, but they are not tests of any kind. Once the application is complete, your documents are in, and the fee is paid, you are ready for the part of the process where you actually have to pass something.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The two permit tests","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-R01","sec02-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"The knowledge test or tests.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-R01","sec02-F11"]},{"text":"A vision test.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-R01","sec02-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"After the paperwork, you must pass your knowledge test or tests plus a vision test. These are the two kinds of passes the permit demands. The knowledge test checks what you have learned from the handbook, and the vision test checks your eyesight. Put the whole permit path together and it has five ordered steps: the application, the documents, the fee, the knowledge tests, and the vision test. The full list of permit steps and requirements is kept on the DMV instruction permit page, which is the best place to confirm anything specific to your case before you go.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-R01","sec02-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Paperwork is not a test","fact_ids":["sec02-R03","sec02-R01","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: counting the fee as a step you pass.","fact_ids":["sec02-R03","sec02-R01","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},{"text":"Truth: only knowledge and vision are tests.","fact_ids":["sec02-R03","sec02-R01","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. Some learners list every step of the permit process as a test, as if paying the fee or handing over documents were something you pass or fail. The handbook draws a clear line. The permit demands two test passes, knowledge and vision, while the documents and the fee are paperwork rather than tests. Another trap is reaching for the drive test too early. If you have no license, the permit comes before any drive test, so the behind-the-wheel test is not part of getting the permit at all. Keep the order and the categories straight.","fact_ids":["sec02-R03","sec02-R01","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-R03","sec02-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Paperwork is done.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-R03","sec02-R01"]},{"text":"What two passes remain?","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-R03","sec02-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: the application is complete and the fee is paid. What two passes remain before the permit is issued? Think it through. The answer is the knowledge test or tests and the vision test. Those are the only two tests in the permit process; the application, documents, and fee are paperwork. If you answered with the drive test, remember that the drive test comes later, after the permit. If you named knowledge and vision, you have the order right: form, documents, fee, and then the two tests that earn the instruction permit.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-R03","sec02-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Five steps in order","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R03","sec02-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Application, documents, fee.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R03","sec02-F11"]},{"text":"Knowledge tests, vision test.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R03","sec02-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us review the permit path. Without a license, you hold an instruction permit before any drive test. The Class C permit starts with a completed Driver's License and ID Card Application, then you hand over documents and pay a non-refundable fee, and then you pass your knowledge test or tests plus a vision test. Only those last two are tests; the rest is paperwork. The full list of steps and requirements lives on the DMV instruction permit page. Next, we look at the extra rules that apply when the permit applicant is under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R03","sec02-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u03","module_id":"sec02-m03","objective_ids":["sec02-u03"],"title":{"text":"Teen permit rules and schools","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},"why_how":[{"text":"A minor who skips one requirement, such as the parent signature, cannot get or use the permit.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},{"text":"Checking the instructor's ID card confirms the training comes from a proper source.","fact_ids":["sec02-F16"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Mia is fifteen and a half, has finished driver education, and wants to start practicing the day her permit arrives.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F15"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Her parent signed the application and accepted financial responsibility, but the permit cannot be used until behind-the-wheel training begins with an instructor who validates it.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},"result":{"text":"Mia waits for her first training lesson, where the instructor validates the permit, and then she may use it.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a minor may drive with a new permit the day it is issued.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]},"correction":{"text":"The minor may not use the permit until behind-the-wheel training begins with an instructor who validates it.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Fifteen and a half, education done, parent signs, instructor validates.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A minor's permit has arrived, but training has not started. May the minor use it yet?","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]},"answer":{"text":"No, not until training begins with an instructor who validates it.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]},"rationale":{"text":"The permit becomes usable only when behind-the-wheel training starts and the instructor validates it.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"When the applicant is a teen","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Extra rules apply under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},{"text":"Age, education, signature, training.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers the extra permit rules for applicants under eighteen. A minor follows the same basic permit steps as anyone else, but several requirements are added. There is a minimum age, a driver education program to finish, a parent or guardian signature, and a rule about when the permit can actually be used. We will also look at where driver education and training come from and how to check that an instructor is properly licensed. Each rule is simple on its own, but together they form a checklist that a teen and a parent need to work through before practice begins.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Age and education","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"At least fifteen and a half.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},{"text":"Finish a driver education program.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Applicants under eighteen must be at least fifteen and a half years old to get an instruction permit. That is the first rung. Those minors must also finish a driver education program. Age alone is not enough, and the education program alone is not enough; both are needed. Notice that the permit age of fifteen and a half is different from the age needed for the license itself, which comes later in the course. For now, lock in the permit rule: a minor must be at least fifteen and a half and must have finished driver education before the permit is issued.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Signature and validation","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Parent or guardian signs.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},{"text":"Both sign under joint custody.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},{"text":"Instructor validates the permit.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"A parent or guardian must sign the minor's application, and by signing they accept financial responsibility. Under joint custody, both parents must sign. Even once the permit is issued, the minor may not use it right away. The permit cannot be used until behind-the-wheel training begins with an instructor who validates it. So the order is application signed by a parent or guardian, permit issued, and then training begins and the instructor validates the permit. Only after that validation does the permit let the minor practice.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Driving on day one","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: the new permit is usable at once.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F14"]},{"text":"Truth: wait for training and validation.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a common mistake. A minor receives the instruction permit and assumes it can be used for practice that same day. The handbook says otherwise. The minor may not use the permit until behind-the-wheel training begins with an instructor who validates it. Until that happens, the permit is not yet usable. Another trap is thinking one parent's signature is always enough. Under joint custody, both parents must sign the application. Keep both rules in view: both signatures where custody is shared, and no practice until the instructor has validated the permit.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"The permit has arrived.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]},{"text":"Training has not started yet.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a minor's instruction permit has arrived in the mail, but behind-the-wheel training has not started. May the minor use the permit yet? Decide first. The answer is no. The minor may not use the permit until behind-the-wheel training begins with an instructor who validates it. Receiving the permit is not the same as being allowed to use it. If you answered correctly, you have one of the most commonly missed teen rules. If not, remember that the instructor's validation at the start of training is what makes the permit usable.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Schools and instructors","fact_ids":["sec02-F16","sec02-F17","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Licensed schools and some high schools.","fact_ids":["sec02-F16","sec02-F17","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]},{"text":"Ask to see the instructor ID card.","fact_ids":["sec02-F16","sec02-F17","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"To finish, driver education and training come from DMV-licensed driving schools and some high schools.
